Date: Mon, 5 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Defining success signals and the go/no-go ladder for our evaluation

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We discussed running a 6-week evaluation focused on two primary outcomes: 1) a 45% reduction in triage time for clinical notes search, and 2) an F1 > 0.72 on entity extraction for the subset of oncology notes. Before we spin up the pilot, procurement and our clinical leads asked for a concrete runbook that clearly defines: success signals, exit gates, and acceptance tests — i.e., what constitutes a pass vs. a fail at each milestone.

Could you (or someone on your team) share a single-sheet MAP that ties milestones to owners, test scripts, and rollback triggers? Procurement also wants a short list of artifacts they can review (SLO table, data retention note, and a short canary checklist).

Attaching a loose example of the evaluation scope we sketched internally.

Appreciate it — Julie
Julie Park
Head of Clinical Ops, OliveHealth
attachments: scope_outline.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Defining success signals and the go/no-go ladder for our evaluation

Julie — thanks for the clear ask. I put Ben and Marissa on copy; they'll help operationalize the tests and the MAP spreadsheet. High-level plan below, and I attached a first draft MAP + an acceptance_tests CSV.

High-level acceptance ladder (proposal):
- Week 0 (onboarding): infra & security check complete; sample data ingestion validated (smoke).
- Week 1–2 (baseline runs): generate baseline throughput and latency numbers; basic QA set (50 seed cases) to validate functional parity.
- Week 3–4 (scale & quality): run full evaluation dataset; measure triage time improvement and entity F1.
- Week 5 (canary): 5% real traffic routing to model variant with caching + quantization profile; monitor error-rate/latency.
- Week 6 (signoff): final run, pass/fail decision based on the KCI thresholds below.

Proposed hard exit gates (fail-fast triggers):
- Safety/fabrication: any PII leakage detected in outputs -> immediate halt and rollback.
- SLO breach: median latency > 1.5s above agreed baseline for 3 consecutive hours during canary.
- Quality drop: entity F1 < 0.65 on the evaluation set at any stage after Week 2.

Key acceptance tests included in CSV: inference concordance checks, sample-level hallucination audit, throughput smoke, and end-to-end triage run timing.

Next steps: Ben will populate the MAP owners and test owners; Marissa will draft the procurement-friendly artifact list (SLO table + retention note). Can we do a 30-min alignment call Thu morning?

— Vivek
Director, Product (Inference)
Redwood Inference
attachments: OliveHealth_MAP_v0.1.xlsx, acceptance_tests.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Defining success signals and the go/no-go ladder for our evaluation

Julie / Vivek — adding specifics on the tests so procurement has clarity and OE (owner + estimated effort). I pulled from our internal runbook and adapted it to OliveHealth's targets. Key test summaries: 

1) Ingestion smoke (owner: Ben) — verifies sample load, schema conformance, basic tokenization parity. Pass = all files processed, <3% dropped. Est: 2 engineer-days.

2) Concordance check (owner: Marissa) — run a deterministic prompt set (200 cases) against baseline model and the candidate model. Pass = >= 95% structural match on critical fields (diagnosis codes, dates). Est: 3 engineer-days.

3) Entity F1 validation (owner: OliveHealth data science, with Redwood support) — run labeled test set (n=1,200). Pass = F1 >= 0.72. Fail => move to remediation sprint (root cause: prompt/label drift or model quantization). Est: 5 eng-days + Olive DS effort.

4) Triage time E2E measurement (owner: OliveHealth product) — instrument the pipeline to measure human triage time for a 200-case sample. Pass = >= 45% reduction vs baseline within statistical significance. Est: 4 eng-days.

5) Canary safety gate (owner: Marissa) — 5% live traffic for 48h window. Pass = no safety alerts, error-rate delta < 0.2% vs baseline, latency median within SLO. Fail = immediate rollback and postmortem.

I added acceptance criteria in the CSV and annotated who signs each gate. Also included a short KMS note for procurement in the MAP workbook.

For Thu call, I can present the test cadence and the minimal artifacts procurement asked for (SLO table, retention policy, test scripts).

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
